## What this region is

The core of @inixiative/transitions: declaring an entity's lifecycle as data (resource -> action -> Action { paths } -> Transition { from, to } -> Side) and asking it the two questions it answers: can this change happen (checkTransition, with checkPath underneath and a structured Reason) and what can happen (available for one record, eligible as a Prisma plan for every record), plus what the package deliberately does not do.

## What it exists for

- Declaring an entity's lifecycle rules as data
- Deciding what belongs in a transition rule and what stays in code
- Deciding whether a proposed change may happen
- Handling a refused change
- Finding out what changes are open, for one record or for all
- Making the set query agree with the single check

## When this is not your domain

These mention this region's words but belong elsewhere; the answer is no, and the region named answers instead.

- only the requester may cancel their own inquiry → transition-authorization
- plug our rebac schema and schema map into the guard → transition-authorization
- push the reviewer onto the approvals array when approving → tenant-stored-transitions
- validate a tenant's edited lifecycle before saving it → tenant-stored-transitions
- can this transition be stored in the database → tenant-stored-transitions
